---
title: Dynamic colour, from a wallpaper this machine does not have
version: 1
---

**From Android 12, a phone can hand an app a colour scheme made from its wallpaper**, and
`dynamicLightColorScheme(context)` is how the app takes it. The planner's theme does that when
`dynamicColor` is true and the phone runs Android 12 or later, API 31, `Build.VERSION_CODES.S`; on
anything older it falls back to the planner's own green. `dynamicColor` defaults to `false` in
`PlannerTheme`, so the brand colours are what the app shows unless somebody decides otherwise.

Which to use is a product decision rather than a technical one.
**Dynamic colour makes the app match the phone; your own scheme makes the app recognisable.** A
study planner might reasonably pick either. What it cannot do is assume dynamic colour exists:
`minSdk` is 26, and five Android versions have no wallpaper colours to give.

A test can ask for both cases, because Robolectric lets one method run as a different Android
version with `@Config(sdk = …)`:

```kotlin
// app/src/test/java/com/example/planner/DynamicColorTest.kt
package com.example.planner

import androidx.compose.material3.MaterialTheme
import androidx.compose.material3.Surface
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.luminance
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.toArgb
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createComposeRule
import androidx.compose.ui.test.onRoot
import com.example.planner.ui.WeekSummary
import com.example.planner.ui.theme.PlannerTheme
import com.github.takahirom.roborazzi.captureRoboImage
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
@Config(qualifiers = "w360dp-h260dp-xhdpi")
class DynamicColorTest {
    @get:Rule val rule = createComposeRule()

    @Test fun onAndroid15() {
        rule.setContent {
            PlannerTheme(dynamicColor = true) {
                val s = MaterialTheme.colorScheme
                println("primary on SDK 35: #%08X".format(s.primary.toArgb()))
                val (hi, lo) = listOf(s.onPrimaryContainer.luminance(), s.primaryContainer.luminance()).sortedDescending()
                println("onPrimaryContainer on primaryContainer: %.2f:1".format((hi + 0.05) / (lo + 0.05)))
                Surface { WeekSummary(planned = 210, done = 70) }
            }
        }
        rule.onRoot().captureRoboImage("shots/week-dynamic.png")
    }

    @Test @Config(sdk = [30]) fun onAndroid11() {
        rule.setContent {
            PlannerTheme(dynamicColor = true) {
                println("primary on SDK 30: #%08X".format(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary.toArgb()))
            }
        }
        rule.waitForIdle()
    }
}
```

```
ana@vm:~/planner$ ./gradlew --console=plain recordRoborazziDebug --tests '*.DynamicColorTest' 2>&1 | grep -E '^BUILD|FAILED'
BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 35s
ana@vm:~/planner$ grep -h -e "SDK " -e "[0-9]:1$" app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest/TEST-com.example.planner.DynamicColorTest.xml | sed "s/.*CDATA\[//"
primary on SDK 30: #FF2F6F4E
primary on SDK 35: #FF2A4174
onPrimaryContainer on primaryContainer: 4.67:1
```

On Android 11, SDK 30, the branch is skipped and `primary` is the planner's own `#FF2F6F4E`. On
Android 15 it is `#FF2A4174`, a blue nobody wrote. **Read that blue carefully: it did not come
from a wallpaper.** Robolectric has none. It is whatever Robolectric's copy of Android 15 holds in
place of one, and on a phone the value would be different for every person. What the test proves is
the mechanism: the branch runs on 31 and up, and the screen is drawn entirely from the scheme it
returns.

```schooling-figure
{"image": "data:image/png;base64,", "alt": "The week summary in a blue scheme: a pale surface, a mid-blue card with white text, a dark blue Add session button and an outlined See courses button.", "caption": "Dynamic colour as Robolectric's Android 15 returned it, with no wallpaper behind it."}
```

The same `WeekSummary`, untouched for the third time, now in blue. **Not run:** dynamic colour on a
phone, with a real wallpaper and the system's colour picker, could not be seen on the recording
machine; Google's documentation on dynamic colour in Compose describes it.

The `println` inside `setContent` is a test's trick and nowhere else's. Composition can run many
times, which is lesson 5's subject, and a composable that prints, logs or writes anything does it
every time.
